# RURO real-data 2016 — post-estimation report (bpool_p3a_v1)

**Date:** 2026-05-29 (Step 4)
**Spec:** bpool_p3a_v1 (55 params; `beta_c=1` numéraire, couples `theta_c=0`)
**Estimates:** real-data 2016 CONOPT, warm start (theta\*); singles_female is
the post-bugfix run. See `RURO_realdata_2016_estimation_v1.md` (Step 3) for
the estimation runs and the `_sm`/`_sf` leisure-suffix fix.
**Generated by:** `RURO_post_estimation_styled.py --report-profile full`
(per-slice HTML + plots under
`EUROMOD-STORAGE/outputs/post_estimation/realdata_2016/{sm2016,sf2016,c2016}/`).

> **Inert-parameter caveat (read first).** Each single-slice / single-year
> estimate identifies only the parameter blocks its data exercises. The
> rest stay at their starting value and appear in the Hessian as exact flat
> (non-positive-eigenvalue) directions. All plots, elasticities, and SEs
> below are built ONLY on the data-identified ("active") block of each
> slice; the inert blocks are listed per slice and must NOT be read as
> estimates. This is expected for slice-wise estimation, not a defect.

## 1. Fit summary

| slice | n_hh | LL | AIC | BIC | ρ²(prior-corrected) | SEs valid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| singles_male   |   766 | −9746.18  | 19602.4 | 20111.4 | 0.111 | 41/55 |
| singles_female (FIXED) |   910 | −11684.84 | 23479.7 | 23998.2 | 0.103 | 47/55 |
| couples        | 2,577 | −60767.13 | 121644.3 | 122340.4 | 0.084 | 49/55 |

- **ρ² is prior-corrected** (against the proposal-prior null, not uniform):
  0.08–0.11. Modest but positive — the structural utility adds explanatory
  power over the B-pool proposal prior. (Uniform-null ρ² is negative
  because the proposal prior already concentrates probability mass; the
  prior-corrected figure is the meaningful one.)
- **Probability fit is exact**: per-household choice probabilities sum to 1
  to machine precision (max error ≤ 4e-16) on all three slices.
- **SEs valid count** (41/47/49 of 55): the invalid ones are exactly the
  inert cross-group params (non-positive Hessian diagonal). All ACTIVE
  params have valid SEs — see §3.

## 2. Structural elasticities (at median X, from estimated θ)

The "elasticities" are Box-Cox curvature heuristics: Hicksian ≈ 1 − θ_l.
They are NOT micro-estimated labor-supply elasticities; treat as preference
curvature summaries.

| group | θ_l | θ_c | β_l(med) | Hicksian | Marshallian | participation | intensive |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Single males   | −0.822 | −0.056 | 0.584 | 1.822 | 1.722 | 0.547 | 1.276 |
| Single females | −0.809 | −0.020 | 0.420 | 1.809 | 1.709 | 0.543 | 1.266 |
| Males in couples | −0.824 | 0.000 | 0.007 | 1.824 | 1.724 | 0.547 | 1.277 |
| Females in couples | −0.767 | 0.000 | 1.722 | 1.767 | 1.667 | 0.530 | 1.237 |

- **θ_l ≈ −0.8 across all four demographic groups** — strikingly stable
  leisure curvature. Couples females are slightly less curved (−0.767).
- **θ_c (singles)** ≈ −0.02 to −0.06: consumption is close to log utility
  (θ_c → 0). Couples θ_c = 0 by spec (fixed).
- The singles_female θ_l, β_l, θ_c here are the **post-bugfix** values
  (`_sf` block). Before the fix they were the male block's numbers.

## 4. Key economic findings

1. **Leisure curvature θ_l ≈ −0.8 is stable across all four groups.** The
   Box-Cox leisure exponent is well below 1 (strongly concave leisure
   utility) and remarkably consistent — a robustness signal for the spec.

2. **`beta_l_nkids_sf = +0.634` (single mothers value leisure more).** This
   female-only n_children leisure effect was SILENTLY DROPPED in the buggy
   singles_female run (the leisure-suffix bug, now fixed) and is recovered
   here. Economically sensible and sizeable.

3. **Wage block is stable and correctly signed across slices:**
   `beta_w0` ≈ 2.17–2.22 (mean log wage), `beta_w_educH` ≈ +0.34
   (positive education premium), `beta_w_pexp` > 0 with `beta_w_pexp2` < 0
   (concave experience profile), `sigma` ≈ 0.40–0.42 (wage dispersion).
   `beta_w_pexp` is correctly signed on real data (it was wrong-signed in
   the synthetic recovery test — see Step 3 finding #1).

4. **`beta_h_pt2` flips sign between single males (−2.11) and single
   females (+0.15)** — men dislike the pt2 hours band, women are roughly
   neutral/slightly positive. Behavioral heterogeneity worth a sentence in
   the paper; both have valid SEs.

5. **Couples region block is identified** (`beta_E_drgn2..8`,
   urban/middle access) — only the couples slice has enough cross-region
   variation to pin these down; on singles they are inert.

## 5. Diagnostics caveats

- **Hessian is non-PD on all slices** (negative eigenvalues = inert
  directions). SEs come from the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse; they are
  valid on the active block but undefined on the inert block (reported as
  invalid, not zero). This is the correct treatment — cf. the
  recovery_test G3b/cov fix (commit c90d47a) which applies the same
  pinv + NaN-on-non-positive-diagonal logic.
- **`economic_sanity` JSON section reports "requires --mnl-base"** even
  though `--mnl-base` was supplied — a gating quirk in the post-estimation
  script (the MU plots `sm_mu.png`, `muc_comparison.png`,
  `mul_comparison.png` and indifference contours DID generate, so the
  marginal-utility substance is present as figures). Minor; logged below.
- **No job/occupation distribution plots** — this spec has
  `occupation choice enabled: False`, so those are correctly inapplicable.
- **No bootstrap CIs** (per session decision). Hessian-pinv SEs on the
  active block are the inference source.
